# task-37f0b9db: sparse 5-marker fill

## Verified recurrence evidence
A confirmed test (3x27) had background 8 and marker color 5. The correct output changed selected 8s to 3 and left all 5 markers intact. Exact correct test output:

```text
8 8 8 8 5 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 5 3 3 3 3 5 3 3 3 3 3 5 8 8
8 5 5 3 3 3 3 3 5 3 3 5 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 5 8 8 8 8 8 8 8
8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 8 5 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 3 5 3 3 5 8 8 8
```

The output's changed cells are precisely the background cells strictly between successive 5 markers along each row, where there are horizontal marker pairs. In the test, this means intervals c4–c13, c13–c18, c18–c24 on row 0 (zero-based, only interior cells changed); row 1 has pairs c1–c2 (adjacent, no fill), c2–c8, c8–c11, c11–c19; row 2 has c11–c20 and c20–c23. Only cells strictly between endpoints become 3; endpoints remain 5; no extrapolation outside marker pairs. This rule exactly produced the accepted output.

## Demo evidence and caution
Demo 1 was 6x28, background 7, marker 5, fill color 3. Clear horizontal pair/sequence examples: row 1 markers at c2,c14,c23 led to fills c3–13 and c15–22; row 2 markers c8,c9,c23 led to fill c10–22; row 4 markers c10,c11,c17 led to fill c12–16. The demo also had fills at c22–23 in rows 3 and 4 despite no obvious same-row right endpoint, apparently related to nearby marker alignment/continuation around the lower-right cluster (rows 3–5, columns 21–24). Thus do not assume the simple same-row rule explains every demo cell; inspect alignments/continuation in the fresh instance. In the accepted test, the simple strictly-between-successive-horizontal-markers rule fully explains the submitted output.

## Procedure for recurrence
1. Identify the dominant background, sparse marker color (known examples: 5), and fill color (known examples: 3); re-derive rather than hardcode colors.
2. On each row, sort marker columns and identify strictly-between intervals; these are strongly evidenced fill locations. Preserve markers and cells outside intervals.
3. Before submitting, check for additional coherent interval continuation associated with nearby rows/marker alignments as seen in the first demo; do not indiscriminately fill all cells right of a marker.
4. Validate exact dimensions and every changed coordinate. The accepted test used no wrong submissions after one demo request."
}
